Mesa 26.2.4's KosmicKrisp (`src/kosmickrisp/compiler/nir_to_msl.c` and `vulkan/kk_shader.c`, SPDX MIT, © LunarG and Google): the pass lists of `msl_preprocess_nir`, `msl_optimize_nir` and `kk_lower_nir` followed in `wgsl_nir.c` (`lower_subpass_dim` after `kk_shader.c`'s), and the printer's shape (a gather, declarations, values predeclared, control flow node by node); lavapipe's `lvp_nir_lower_pipeline_layout.c` (MIT) as the model for lowering `vulkan_resource_index` to an index and offset. The WGSL printing and the descriptor and binding scheme are ours

Mesa 26.2.4's KosmicKrisp (`src/kosmickrisp/vulkan/`, SPDX MIT, © LunarG and Google) as the model for a driver on the runtime's `vk_shader` path (`kk_shader.c`'s `vk_device_shader_ops` and `kk_cmd_bind_shaders`, the dynamic vertex-input state set in the command buffer), and lavapipe's `lvp_device.c` (MIT) for the device's shape; no code copied. The format table follows the WebGPU spec's texture format capabilities (W3C, documentation)

virglrenderer `e0a1caf3b147`: a diff whose context is lines of `src/venus/vkr_{context,device_memory,queue,renderer,ring}.{c,h}` (SPDX MIT, © Google; our changes MIT like the files): vkr's threads replaced by polls, blobs exported as their storage. `vk/wasi/` is Mesa 26.2.4's `os_misc.h` and `os_get_option` signatures with bodies of ours, and stubs for the POSIX headers wasi-libc lacks; `vk/driver/` is ours, written against Mesa's Vulkan runtime (its entrypoint tables generated by Mesa's `vk_entrypoints_gen.py`, MIT)
the engine setup of Tailscale's `cmd/tsconnect/wasm/wasm_js.go` (v1.102.5), with our `Tun` device and JS API instead of the netstack-terminated sockets and ssh; header kept

tailcat v0.7.0 (`github.com/tailscale/tailcat`, `52fbad3`): the address format, read and written (`wire.go`, `ParseAddr` in `tailcat.go`), the meow handshake from both sides (`disco.go`), the tunnel address of a node key (`tcAddrForKey`) and the NAT64 prefix convention; reimplemented in Rust from those files, nothing copied

the control channel's record framing of tailscale-rs's `ts_control_noise` v0.6.1 (`codec.rs`, `handshake.rs`: the 3-byte header, the record types, the chunk size, the counter nonces), rewritten without its tokio codec, and the early payload of `ts_control`'s `connect.rs`; the handshake itself is `ts_noise`'s, a dependency

the control session, map stream and data plane follow tailscale-rs's `ts_control` (`client/register.rs`, `client/map_stream.rs`, `map_request_builder.rs`) and Tailscale's `controlclient`, `magicsock` and `filter` (v1.102.5): what's sent and how responses apply; reimplemented over the worker's transports, nothing copied

the DERP client handshake and frame types of Tailscale's `derp` package as tailscale-rs's `ts_derp` (v0.6.1) has them (`frame/`, `client.rs` `make_clientinfo`); reimplemented over a byte stream, nothing copied

`tailscale.com/control/controlhttp/client_js.go` (v1.102.5), copied with one marked change (keep the control server's HTTPS port over WebSocket); `net/tailscale/build.sh` builds against a copy of the module with this file replaced

xkeyboard-config 2.41 (`symbols/`, compiled with `xkbcomp` as `pc+<layout>(<variant>)`): the characters each layout puts on the keys' four levels, as data; the keysyms' characters from X11's `keysymdef.h` (xorgproto 2023.2, Ubuntu 24.04's x11proto-dev). No code copied

sections.title: Techniques from papers and other projects (ideas, no code)
intro: Reimplemented from the description, nothing copied; credited all the same.

entries.name: Mike Hamburg, "Accelerating AES with Vector Permute Instructions"

md.idea: AES SubBytes by "nested inversion" over the tower field GF(2⁴)[t]/(t² + t + ζ) with 16-entry lookups as vector permutes and an infinity flag; the formulas and field representation of section 3.3, implemented by us (tables generated at compile time)
md.source: Mike Hamburg, "Accelerating AES with Vector Permute Instructions", CHES 2009 (the paper; the technique behind OpenSSL's `vpaes`, whose code we didn't read)

entries.name: Daemen and Rijmen, "The Design of Rijndael"

md.idea: InvMixColumns as MixColumns after a multiply by 04 00 05 00
md.source: Daemen and Rijmen, "The Design of Rijndael", 4.1.3

md.idea: Carry-less multiplication with integer multiplies of operands masked to every fourth bit ("multiply with holes"), so partial sums can't carry into the next bit of the same class; constant time without a carry-less multiply instruction
md.source: Thomas Pornin, BearSSL's `bmul` (`src/hash/ghash_ctmul.c`) and its "Constant-Time Mul" notes (bearssl.org), MIT

md.idea: A NIR → WGSL backend modelled on KosmicKrisp's NIR → MSL (`src/kosmickrisp/compiler/`), with its pass order (`kosmicomp.c`, `vulkan/kk_shader.c`) as the spike's
md.source: KosmicKrisp in Mesa 26.2.4 (SPDX MIT on its files), and LunarG's XDC 2025 overview

md.where: docs/graphics.md "What maps, what's emulated, what isn't offered" (geometry and tessellation, not built)
md.idea: Geometry and tessellation as a compute pre-pass that expands into vertex and index buffers, then a plain draw
md.source: libpoly (Mesa 26.2.4's `src/poly/`, from Asahi and Honeykrisp; SPDX MIT) and its FOSDEM talk on panvk; MoltenVK's tessellation (v1.4.2, Apache-2.0) for the known cost

md.idea: A Venus decoder generated by a `build.rs` from venus-protocol's XML, as virglrenderer's `vkr` and Mesa's Venus driver are generated from it
md.source: [venus-protocol](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/virgl/venus-protocol) v1.1.3 (`ca19b6358d7c`): no LICENSE file; its generator (`vn_protocol.py`, `vkxml.py`, `templates/`) MIT by SPDX tag, its XML (`vk.xml`, `VK_MESA_venus_protocol.xml`, `VK_EXT_command_serialization.xml`) Apache-2.0 OR MIT

intro:
Checked on 2026-09-25 against the upstream default branch at the commit listed; the Vulkan work's rows (VK0,
VK1) on 2026-10-25 at the version or tag listed. Re-check at the commit you actually pin before copying anything.
**Permissive: code may be ported with attribution.**

md.notes: JIT architecture (wasmgen, block compilation and batching), 9p and its lazy HTTP filesystem, state save/restore, async HTTP disks; in-browser comparison target (i686)

`virtio.c`, `fs*.c` and `riscv_*` are MIT. `slirp/` has its own headers. `aes.c`, `sha256.c`, `fbuf.h`, `ps2.h` lack the MIT header, so check them individually. Compact virtio-mmio and virtio devices in C; JSLinux is an in-browser comparison target (riscv64)
Repository **archived** 2024-03. The former upstream (merryhime/dynarmic) is gone. Fine as a read-only reference. The decoder's pattern table; IR design, A64 semantics, JIT techniques

The virgl protocol (`src/virgl_protocol.h`, `virgl_hw.h`), the host's command decoder (`src/vrend/vrend_decode.c`) and TGSI → GLSL translator (`vrend_shader.c`): G3's reference, porting allowed with attribution. A debug build with our capture patch (`tools/virgl-oracle/capture.patch`, a diff against `c8e3fc3b`, MIT like the file it patches) is the oracle (`tools/virgl-oracle/build.sh`, built into `target/`, not distributed)

The Venus renderer (`src/venus/`, `vkr`) behind vtest is VK0's and VK1's oracle (`tools/venus-oracle/`, with `capture.patch`: above), and route (b) plans to build `vkr` for wasm as the translator's decoder (docs/graphics.md "The shape"); its generated decoder comes from venus-protocol v1.1.3 (techniques table)

md.license: MIT for the parts we touch (`docs/license.rst`; SPDX MIT on `src/virtio/vulkan/` (the Venus driver), `src/vulkan/runtime/`, `src/compiler/nir/`, `src/compiler/spirv/`, `src/poly/` (libpoly), `src/kosmickrisp/`, `src/gallium/frontends/lavapipe/`; the runtime's `radix_sort/`, for acceleration structures only, is Fuchsia's BSD-style). Elsewhere other licences (`licenses/`: SGI-B-2.0 for GLX, GPL-2.0-only, BSL-1.0, Apache-2.0)
md.notes: The Venus driver in the oracle (above), lavapipe as the dev VM's Vulkan; route (b) (docs/graphics.md "The shape") is Mesa's common Vulkan runtime, `spirv_to_nir`, NIR's passes and libpoly under a WebGPU backend of ours; VK1 step 1 built the compiler for wasm (the workloads table); KosmicKrisp is also in LunarG's macOS SDK (above)
naga is VK0 D's SPIR-V → WGSL translator and route (a)'s (development dependencies above); wgpu-hal's Vulkan backend read for A (what Firefox's WebGPU asks of a device)

Chromium's WebGPU, which every browser arm of VK0 runs on (Tint compiles our WGSL); A ran it in the guest's role on lavapipe and read what it requires of Vulkan; Tint's SPIR-V reader is route (a)'s other frontend, not tried
Chromium's GL on Vulkan in A (what ES3 needs of a device); on Metal, G's baseline on the Mac
the dev VM's WebGPU adapter (correctness only), the source of A's `webgpu-swiftshader` profile
VK0's native context arm on the Mac; its feature level and tessellation cost a reference for the plan (techniques table)
vkcube, a program measured in A, B and D; `vulkaninfo`
headless sway as the Wayland compositor for VK0's presenting clients (`tools/venus-oracle/wayland.sh`); wlroots's Vulkan renderer read for A; sway 1.12 is also G's compositor in the desktop guest
virtio devices (blk, net, gpu, input, snd), the `p9` crate, arm64 FDT, PSCI; `rutabaga_gfx` for graphics
Needs NOTICE/attribution if code is copied. Minimal virtio-mmio model, arm64 FDT, direct kernel boot
Not used: `core/src/fdt.rs` is our own writer

md.license: virtio-queue: **Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause**; virtio-bindings: BSD-3-Clause OR Apache-2.0
md.notes: Repository **archived** 2026-09-11. Crates are still published. Not used: our own split queues (`core/src/virtio.rs`)
GICv2/GICv3 and generic timer models (M7's per-CPU GIC)
TestFloat vectors (`scripts/testfloat.sh`); the FP suite's reference (`images/fptest`, linked, not copied); the FP core itself is ours
Some parts are LLVM-derived under their own license. We use it only as a tool: the decoder sweep, disassembly for debugging
The Clear variant explicitly grants no patent rights. Executable ISA model: the oracle for disputed corner cases

md.notes: **Read the notice in the downloaded package before generating code from it.** Until then, dynarmic's 0BSD decoder table is the safe source

Tailscale's Rust client: its sans-I/O crates are the tailnet client's dependencies (above); its control, DERP and runtime crates, which need sockets and tokio's runtime, are the reference for ours (docs/tailnet.md "The module")
